correctness.rationale: For the forbidden 2-adic set E, its closure off E is the singleton 0 and its Haar measure is 1/6. A nonzero point of T^{-1}(E) outside E gives a whole cylinder containing a nonnegative integer counterexample; zero is already an input. An odd slope preserves measure, making the inclusion equality almost everywhere: any nonzero preimage of 0 has a neighborhood either inside or outside E but with a mixed preimage of E, a contradiction. Hence b=0 for an odd slope and checking the mod-8 odd classes gives a≡1. A slope 2u with u odd and b odd has preimage measure 1/4, impossible. For b even its 2-adic zero t lies in the closure of E by preimages of high forbidden cylinders, so t is 0,4,7 mod 8. The preimage of 28 mod 32 then has residue t+14/u mod 8, none of 0,4,7, contradiction. Common division by four preserves membership of the output; for the remaining slope divisible by four, outputs 1 or 2 mod 4 always pass, and 3 mod 4 needs a fixed residue 3 mod 8 (otherwise n=0 or 1 fails). This also gives the stated valuation conditions. Disjoint pair buckets give the recurrence, whose main term sums (9/64) times the geometric series of ratio 1/16; floors contribute only O(X) by geometric summation.
residual_risks: The bundled recurrence check samples powers of two through 256, not every box up to 256; general validity is analytical. The O(X) assertion is for positive intercepts only.

value.rationale: This is a complete arithmetic classification for a canonical classical value set, not a list of congruential examples. It separates homogeneous from positive shifts, rules out every slope of dyadic valuation one at the reduced level, and gives an exact count and limiting fraction for all positive pairs.
